name: Polybius
biography: Greek historian (born c. 200 B.C.) taken to Rome as a prisoner, who became fluent in Latin (unusual for a Greek) and wrote, for a Greek audience, a history of the Punic Wars explaining Rome's rise; admired the Roman constitution's stability and efficiency compared to constantly changing Greek city constitutions, though his admiration was becoming outdated even as he wrote.
